title: Beer Distribution Game
transcript: Place the weekly order cards in the order card box. Give each player their matching pad of paper. Take two pieces of paper from each pad, write the number four on them, and place them face down in the orders placed and incoming orders boxes. The factory only needs one piece and places it in their production request box. Put 12 chips in the current inventory and four in each of the shipping delays. The retailer sells beer to the customer. The wholesaler sells beer to the retailer. The distributor sells beer to the wholesaler. And the factory produces beer for the distributor. Each position slides their chips at the same time by placing each hand on a shipping delay box and sliding the chips over one box. The retailer looks at their weekly order card and then takes the needed amount of chips from their current inventory and pushes them up to the customer. The distributor and manufacturer do the same thing. They look at their incoming orders, push the needed amount of chips to the shipping delay, and then slide the orders placed slip to the incoming orders box. The factory checks the incoming orders and pushes the number of cases to the shipping delay. Then they also have to check their production requests and put that number of chips into the production delay from the raw materials. To place orders, you write the amount of cases you would like to receive and place the slip face down in the orders placed box. The retailer, wholesaler, and distributor all do this the same way. To place orders, the factory writes their desired number of cases on a slip and places it in their production requests box. The last step is to fill out your form, and each position does this the same way. Write down the number of cases you have in your current inventory, any amount of backlog you may have, and the number of cases you requested.

title: The Beer Game Explained
transcript: hi there let me explain to you about the beer game which is a popular Topic in supply chain the beer game has been invented in the 1960s by J Forrester at MIT it's an interactive role-play modeling approach that requires players to solve typical supply chain coordination difficulties in the absence of information exchange and cooperation participants in the beer game design a four-stage supply chain the aim is to manufacture and transport beer units from the factory manufacturers and the remaining three stages provide the beer units till they reach the client at the downstream point in the chain the product flows forward from Factory to distributor who sells the products to wholesaler and last but not the least the wholesaler provides it to the retailer whereas the orders move in the opposite direction vice versa from retailer to the manufacturer the game is played assuming orders week wise the goal for the players is to minimize costs inventory and back order costs what is a back order if an incoming order cannot be fully fulfilled due to a lack of available items in the inventory items go on back order in this case your inventory is empty and a number of items will appear as back order in your play sheet what happens in the next week in the following week the old back order will be added to the new incoming order again if the available inventory is too small to fulfill the outstanding order amount items will be put on back order no communication is allowed between players must not talk to each other at any time especially the customer demand is only known to the retailer penalty at the cost of inventory carry low inventory as possible inventory a backlog is recorded on the log sheet decision to make orders is crucial foreign
